questions.stem:
Consider the following reaction.
4-BrC₆H₄CH₂OH —red phosphorous, Br₂→ R (major product)
On estimation of bromine in 1.00 g of R using Carius method, the amount of AgBr formed (in g) is ________.
[Given: Atomic mass of H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, P = 31, Br = 80, Ag = 108]
questions.solution: Red P and Br₂ generate PBr₃, which replaces the benzylic OH by Br; the aryl C–Br bond is untouched, so R is 4-BrC₆H₄CH₂Br, C₇H₆Br₂ (M = 250). 1.00 g of R = 0.004 mol, which contains 0.008 mol Br. In the Carius method all of it ends up as AgBr (M = 188): 0.008 × 188 = 1.504 g ≈ 1.50 g.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
The weight percentage of hydrogen in Q, formed in the following reaction sequence, is ________.
C₆H₅Cl —1. NaOH, 623 K, 300 atm 2. conc. H₂SO₄ and then conc. HNO₃→ Q (major product)
[Given: Atomic mass of H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, S = 32, Cl = 35]
questions.solution: Fusing chlorobenzene with NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm (Dow process) gives sodium phenoxide, and from it phenol. Sulfonation followed by nitration with conc. HNO₃ replaces the SO₃H groups and gives picric acid, 2,4,6-trinitrophenol, C₆H₃N₃O₇ (M = 229). %H = 3/229 × 100 = 1.31%.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
If the reaction sequence given below is carried out with 15 moles of acetylene, the amount of the product D formed (in g) is ________.
HC≡CH —iron tube (red hot)→ A (80%) —H₃C–CH₂–CH₂–Cl, AlCl₃→ B (50%) —1. O₂ 2. H₃O⁺, −CH₃COCH₃→ C (50%) —CH₃COCl, pyridine→ D (100%)
The yields of A, B, C and D are given in parentheses.
[Given: Atomic mass of H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Cl = 35]
questions.solution: Three acetylenes cyclise to benzene: 15/3 × 0.8 = 4 mol of A. Friedel–Crafts alkylation with 1-chloropropane goes through rearrangement to the isopropyl cation, giving cumene: 4 × 0.5 = 2 mol of B. The cumene process (O₂, then H₃O⁺, with loss of acetone) gives phenol: 2 × 0.5 = 1 mol of C. Acetylation in pyridine gives phenyl acetate, C₈H₈O₂ (M = 136): 1 mol = 136 g of D.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
Considering the reaction sequence given below, the correct statement(s) is(are)
CH₃CH₂COOH —1. Br₂, red phosphorous 2. H₂O→ P —1. potassium phthalimide 2. NaOH 3. H₃O⁺→ Q + phthalic acid

options.text: P can be reduced to a primary alcohol using NaBH₄.
Treating P with conc. NH₄OH solution followed by acidification gives Q.
Treating Q with a solution of NaNO₂ in aq. HCl liberates N₂.
P is more acidic than CH₃CH₂COOH.

questions.solution: HVZ bromination gives 2-bromopropanoic acid (P). Gabriel synthesis (N-alkylation of phthalimide, then hydrolysis) gives alanine (Q) and phthalic acid. (A) NaBH₄ does not reduce a carboxylic acid, so it is false. (B) Ammonolysis of the α-bromo acid with conc. NH₄OH, then acidification, also gives alanine, so it is true. (C) Alanine is a primary aliphatic amine and gives N₂ with HNO₂, so it is true. (D) The −I effect of the α-Br makes P stronger than propanoic acid, so it is true.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
Considering the following reaction sequence,
4-nitrotoluene —P→ Q —R→ S —H₂O→ T; S —U→ benzoic acid
the correct option(s) is(are)

options.text: P = H₂/Pd, ethanol; R = NaNO₂/HCl; U = 1. H₃PO₂ 2. KMnO₄–KOH, heat
P = Sn/HCl; R = HNO₂; S = 4-methylbenzenediazonium chloride (p-CH₃C₆H₄N₂⁺Cl⁻)
S = 4-methylbenzenediazonium chloride (p-CH₃C₆H₄N₂⁺Cl⁻); T = 4-methylphenol (p-cresol); U = 1. CH₃CH₂OH 2. KMnO₄–KOH, heat
Q = 4-nitrobenzoic acid; R = H₂/Pd, ethanol; T = 4-methylphenol (p-cresol)

questions.solution: The route is: reduce NO₂ to NH₂ (P: H₂/Pd or Sn/HCl) to get p-toluidine (Q), diazotise (R: NaNO₂/HCl, i.e. HNO₂) to get 4-methylbenzenediazonium chloride (S), and warm with water to get p-cresol (T). To reach benzoic acid, the N₂⁺ group is first removed by H₃PO₂ or ethanol, giving toluene, and the methyl group is then oxidised by hot alkaline KMnO₄. So (A), (B) and (C) are consistent. (D) fails: if Q were 4-nitrobenzoic acid, H₂/Pd would only give 4-aminobenzoic acid, and the sequence could not lead to p-cresol.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
Match the compounds in LIST-I with the observations in LIST-II, and choose the correct option.
LIST-I
(I) Aniline
(II) o-Cresol
(III) Cysteine
(IV) Caprolactam
LIST-II
(P) Sodium fusion extract of the compound on boiling with FeSO₄, followed by acidification with conc. H₂SO₄, gives Prussian blue color.
(Q) Sodium fusion extract of the compound on treatment with sodium nitroprusside gives blood red color.
(R) Addition of the compound to a saturated solution of NaHCO₃ results in effervescence.
(S) The compound reacts with bromine water to give a white precipitate.
(T) Treating the compound with neutral FeCl₃ solution produces violet color.
questions.solution: Aniline contains N, so its Lassaigne extract gives Prussian blue (P), and with bromine water it gives white 2,4,6-tribromoaniline (S). o-Cresol is a phenol and gives a violet colour with neutral FeCl₃ (T). Cysteine contains both N and S, and the sulfur test on its fusion extract is the one listed as (Q); its free COOH liberates CO₂ from NaHCO₃ (R). Caprolactam contains N, so it gives (P). Only option (D) matches.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper
